title: Finite-flat groupoid presentations and their invariant open substacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, and 2-fibre products have the meanings in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], with $s,t$ finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Suppose its fppf quotient stack $\mathcal Q=[U/R]$ is Deligne--Mumford. Here the quotient is the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $U(T)$-objects and $R(T)$-arrows [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. The natural map $p:U\to\mathcal Q$ is representable by schemes, surjective, finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. Pullback along $p$ gives a bijection between strictly full open substacks $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal Q$ and open subschemes $V\subseteq U$ satisfying $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$. Such a substack satisfies $U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal V=V$ and $\mathcal V\simeq[V/R_V]$, where $R_V=R\times_{U\times_S U}(V\times_S V)$. The restricted projections $R_V\rightrightarrows V$ are finite locally free, and $V\to\mathcal V$ is again representable, surjective, finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. The map $|U|\to|\mathcal Q|$ is surjective. If $U$ is affine, then $\mathcal Q$ is absolutely separated: its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is proper. Here an open substack means a full substack stable under pullback whose scheme base changes are open subschemes. Finite, flat and locally of finite presentation are tested after scheme base change using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; proper for a representable diagonal means proper on scheme charts [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: By [def-pc-finite-locally-free], both projections are finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] to the given groupoid over the given scheme $S$. It gives an algebraic stack $\mathcal Q$, an algebraic-space-representable, surjective, flat, locally finitely presented map $p:U\to\mathcal Q$, and the canonical identification $R\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$ with projections $s,t$. No smoothness of $s,t$, no field base and no constant-rank assumption are required.

Fix an affine scheme $T$ and an object $x:T\to\mathcal Q$, and put $F=T\times_{\mathcal Q}U$, initially an algebraic space. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], choose an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and maps $u_i:T_i\to U$ with $x|_{T_i}\simeq p(u_i)$. The relation in step 1 identifies $F\times_TT_i\to T_i$ with a base change of one of $s,t$. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], hence affine by the definition of finite morphism. Apply the affine clause of [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent] to $F\to T$ and this fppf family. Thus $F\to T$ is affine; since $T$ is affine, $F$ itself is an affine scheme. The same family is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] applies to the scheme morphism $F\to T$ and proves that it is finite. In particular we use scheme finiteness descent only after obtaining scheme representability.

source.place: Tag 0DUM (lemma-well-nigh-affine), descent of finiteness in its proof; spaces-descent.tex Tag 041Z (lemma-descending-property-affine); descent.tex Tag 02LA (lemma-descending-property-finite).

proof.text: For an arbitrary scheme $T\to\mathcal Q$, the pullbacks over its affine open cover are the affine finite schemes of step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens] to these schemes and their canonical restriction maps. The resulting scheme represents $T\times_{\mathcal Q}U$: the identifications are identities on the represented fibre-product sheaves, so satisfy the cocycle. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target], its projection to $T$ is finite. Hence $p$ is representable by schemes and finite, in addition to the properties in step 1. Surjectivity of $|p|$ is exactly the field-extension lifting clause of [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient]: for any field-valued object of $\mathcal Q$, the lifted field-valued point of $U$ has the same class in $|\mathcal Q|$.

source.place: Tag 0DUM (lemma-well-nigh-affine), proof; morphisms.tex Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local); criteria.tex Tag 06FH (lemma-flat-quotient-flat-presentation).

proof.text: If $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal Q$ is an open substack, its pullback $V=U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W$ is an open subscheme by the definition of open substack. Under $R=U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$ from [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient], the two maps $R\to\mathcal Q$ are isomorphic. Strict fullness of $\mathcal W$ then identifies their inverse images of $\mathcal W$, giving $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$.

Conversely let $V\subseteq U$ be invariant. For $x:T\to\mathcal Q$, choose local lifts $u_i:T_i\to U$ as in step 2. On $T_i\times_TT_j$, the comparison between their images in $\mathcal Q$ is an arrow of $R=U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$ by [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient]. Invariance gives equal inverse images of $V$ under its two endpoints. Thus the opens $u_i^{-1}(V)$ agree on overlaps. The fppf family is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]; [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] gives a unique open $W_x\subseteq T$ pulling back to these opens. Uniqueness, applied on common refinements, makes $W_x$ independent of the lifts and compatible with every scheme pullback and every isomorphism of $x$. Define $\mathcal W(T)$ to be the full subgroupoid of objects $x$ for which $W_x=T$. This is a strictly full substack: the property is local and invariant under isomorphism, so descent in $\mathcal Q$ restricts to it. For a map $a:T'\to T$, the object $x|_{T'}$ is in $\mathcal W$ exactly when $a^{-1}(W_x)=T'$, equivalently when $a$ factors through the open $W_x$. This proves $T\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W=W_x$ and proves that $\mathcal W$ is open. Taking a lift from $U$ itself proves $U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W=V$.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), descent argument applied to the fppf cover; descent.tex Tag 03N0 (lemma-open-fpqc-covering).

proof.text: These constructions are inverse. Starting from an open $\mathcal W$, its pullback to every $T_i$ is $u_i^{-1}(V)$, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] identifies $W_x$ with $T\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W$. Hence the full subgroupoid constructed in step 5 is the original one. Starting from $V$, the last assertion of step 5 recovers $V$ itself. This gives the asserted bijection, not merely existence of an open image.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), bijectivity in the open case.

proof.text: An open substack $\mathcal W$ of the given Deligne--Mumford stack is again Deligne--Mumford: restrict an etale surjective scheme atlas of $\mathcal Q$ to its open inverse image, and restrict the representable diagonal. Every scheme test of the restricted atlas is the identical test of the original atlas, since $\mathcal W$ is a full substack; thus it is etale and surjective. The square with $V,U,\mathcal W,\mathcal Q$ is cartesian, so $V\to\mathcal W$ is a base change of $p$. On every scheme test, finiteness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], and flatness, local finite presentation and surjectivity by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. In the groupoid, invariance identifies $R_V=R\times_{U\times_SU}(V\times_SV)$ with both $s^{-1}(V)$ and $t^{-1}(V)$. Thus each restricted projection is a base change of the corresponding original projection; the same permanence results and [def-pc-finite-locally-free] give finite local freeness. Finally $V\times_{\mathcal W}V=R_V$ by reassociation of these cartesian squares. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations] to the representable surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme map $V\to\mathcal W$. It gives $[V/R_V]\simeq\mathcal W$, commuting with the object map.

Assume $U$ affine and work absolutely over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Put $C=U\times_{\mathbf Z}U$. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], so its projection $C\to U$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. The arrow map $j=(s,t):R\to C$ has composite with the first projection equal to the finite morphism $s$. This composite is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Apply [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] to the triangle $R\to C\to U$. It proves $j$ proper. This uses the absolute product $C$, not $U\times_SU$, and needs no separatedness hypothesis on $S$.

source.place: Tag 0DTY (lemma-properties-diagonal-from-presentation), proof of (6); schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); morphisms.tex Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper).

proof.text: Consider the absolute diagonal $\Delta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q\times_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal Q$. Regard the groupoid as an absolute groupoid by forgetting its $S$-structure; this does not change its total quotient stack or its self-relation $R$. Algebraicity and the relation calculation of [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] therefore also apply over $\mathbf Z$. The product target is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. The map $p\times p:C\to\mathcal Q\times_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal Q$ is a composite of two base changes of $p$, so is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Its base change of $\Delta$ is exactly $j:R\to C$, by the self-relation identification: a pair of objects of $U$ together with an isomorphism in $\mathcal Q$ is an arrow of $R$. The diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-proper-fppf-target-test] to $\Delta$ and this scheme cover $C$. Since $j$ is proper by step 8, $\Delta$ is proper. This proves absolute separatedness.

Steps 1-3 obtain p finite and representable by schemes in the right order: local lifts, then fppf descent of affineness for algebraic spaces, so the pullback is an affine scheme, and only then fpqc descent of finiteness for schemes, followed by Zariski gluing. Steps 4-6 prove the invariant-open bijection directly by fpqc descent of opens. They avoid the smooth-atlas node lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent, which would not apply because a finite flat p is not smooth. Step 7 establishes every hypothesis of clause (2) of fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations before using it. Steps 8-9 are the 0DTY(5)/(6) argument: R -> U x_Z U is proper by the proper-triangle criterion, then the fppf target test applies to the absolute diagonal. I checked that isomorphisms in Q lie over the identity of the test scheme, so the pullback of the diagonal along p x p is j : R -> U x_Z U even when S is not separated. Small cases tested: the identity groupoid, the empty groupoid, BG for a finite constant group in characteristic dividing its order, and a nonseparated base S.
